# jev-notetaker

> Finds which qualities of your writing actually predict engagement. It analyses
> published posts and never generates them; the underlying model cannot write.

jev-notetaker rates every post you have published against a pre-registered
rubric using Jev, TypeSafe AI's System One model, then tests those ratings
against your real engagement data. It reports findings in plain language and
withholds conclusions when the sample is too small to support them.

## What it is

- A command-line tool and agent skill, MIT licensed, Node >= 20.
- Bring your own key: Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, or TypeSafe direct.
- LinkedIn is the first adapter; rubric packs make other platforms user-space files.

## What makes it different from an LLM rating your posts

- Jev returns calibrated probability distributions rather than generated scores,
  so a rubric whose confidence sits near 0.5 across a corpus can be detected as
  broken rather than silently reported.
- Every question is pre-registered in git as primary or exploratory before any
  result is seen, and the commit timestamp is the evidence.
- Below 25 posts with outcome data the tool refuses to correlate at all and
  shows descriptive statistics only.
- Headline results are re-tested as partial correlations controlling for
  publication date, because a rated dimension and an outcome that both drift
  over time will correlate for no reason.
- Countable features such as length, emoji, hashtags and posting cadence are
  computed in code and compete with the model's judgments on equal footing.

## Two outcomes it keeps separate

- reach rate = impressions divided by follower count at post time. Did the
  platform distribute it?
- conversion rate = engagements divided by impressions. Given that people saw
  it, did the writing work? This is unconfounded by follower count and feed luck.

## Key files

- README: https://github.com/Kaos599/jev-notetaker#readme
- Rubric pack format and validation: src/rubrics/pack.mjs
- Statistics and the power gate: src/stats.mjs
- Plain-language report layer: src/report.mjs
- LinkedIn export adapter: src/adapters/linkedin.mjs
